title: Add benchmark-lab adaptive batching runners, profiling baselines, and reporting pipeline
author: Asha Menon
description:
Motivation: add adaptive-batching representative workload runners and new profiling baselines to better measure tail-latency vs throughput trade-offs for mixed sequence-length workloads. Also extend the benchmark lab reporting pipeline to ingest the new baseline artifacts and emit per-run breakdowns (batch size distribution, KV cache hit rates, prefix reuse).

What this PR does: adds an adaptive batching runner that simulates heterogeneous client requests (short/long seq mixes), a set of profiling baseline configs (cold/warm/kv-cache scenarios), and upgrades the reporting DAG to accept the new runner outputs and generate aggregated charts and CSV summaries consumed by the performance dashboard. Includes metric exporter changes so the reporting pipeline can reconcile run metadata with Prometheus labels.

Checklist: 
- [x] adaptive batching runner implementation (Python)
- [x] profiling baseline configs and example workload definitions
- [x] reporting DAG changes + smaller schema migration for reporting store
- [x] unit tests for runner logic and baseline parsers
- [x] docs snippet in benchmark-lab/README.md summarizing how to run the new workloads

Notes: the schema change is additive (new columns: batch_size_histogram, kv_cache_hit_rate) and backwards compatible with existing reports. The CI flake previously seen in pipeline tests was due to a mocked time dependency; tests updated to use freezegun. Related Linear tickets are ENG-4821 (adaptive batching) and ENG-4893 (reporting ingestion). Support ticket SUP-1198 requested clearer cold-start baselines from a customer load test.

release_notes: Add adaptive-batching representative workload runner, new profiling baselines (cold/warm/kv-cache), and reporting pipeline ingestion for batch histograms and KV cache metrics. Adds configs and docs for running mixed-sequence benchmarks.
